items.title: Norfolk and Suffolk ICB sizes its CVD prevention and optimisation service at £12.4m
items.summary: NHS Norfolk and Suffolk Integrated Care Board has published a second market engagement notice for a single, digitally enabled cardiovascular disease prevention and optimisation pathway, starting with hypertension and lipid management, at an estimated £12.4m.

items.title: STRIDE-RCT: cancer-detecting blood tests to be offered to 20,000 NHS patients via 200 GP practices
items.summary: The STRIDE-RCT trial will offer blood tests for early cancer signals to over 20,000 patients aged 45+ with abdominal symptoms at 200 GP surgeries. First tests: Proteotype (Enlighten), Pinpoint AI (PinPoint) and Mercy Bioanalytics (Halo); more may be added. Source: Evening Standard.

items.title: NMC warns AI-generated referrals are complicating fitness to practise assessments
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used in fitness to practise (FtP) referrals and is, in some cases, making it difficult for the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) to assess whether regulatory action is needed.

items.title: GPs should be reimbursed for hosting district nurses, MPs urge
items.summary: The government must ensure GP practices are reimbursed for hosting other professions such as district nurses and community services if it wants its neighbourhood shift to succeed, an influential committee of MPs has urged.

items.title: NHS Property Services should face ‘independent review’, say MPs
items.summary: The Government has been urged to commission a review into NHS Property Services (NHSPS) due to ‘consistent concerns’ about its ownership of GP practice premises.

items.title: Government urged to create loan scheme for GPs to invest in premises upgrades
items.summary: The Government has been urged to give GPs access to Government-backed borrowing to help GPs invest in premises upgrades, as part of a ‘GP capital and revenue investment strategy’.

items.title: NMC drops plans to reduce nursing programme hours
items.summary: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) has dropped plans to change student nursing programme hours after a consultation revealed a lack of support.

items.title: Managing hyperkalaemia – five top tips for GPs
items.summary: As part of our series showcasing Pulse LIVE and Virtual sessions highlights, GP diabetes specialist Dr Kevin Fernando provides five practical pointers on how to manage a case of hyperkalaemia Note the case discussed in this article is fictional and created for educational purposes Hyperkalaemia is commonly encountered…

items.title: Sleep disorders: Top ten advice and guidance requests
items.summary: Consultant neurologist Dr Kirstie Anderson, consultant in sleep and respiratory medicine Dr Alanna Hare and GP Dr Elspeth Wise discuss ten typical requests to advice and guidance for sleep disorders and how they should be managed Note all 10 requests are fictional and developed for educational purposes 1.

items.title: First cross-party parliamentary group dedicated to nursing launched
items.summary: A cross-party parliamentary group dedicated to the nursing profession has been launched for the first time. The All-Party Parliamentary Group (APPG) for Nursing has been established in Westminster, with MPs and nurses coming together for an inaugural meeting this week to discuss priorities and issues raised by nurses.

items.title: Government seeks nurse views on proposed NHS Pension Scheme changes
items.summary: Nurses and other healthcare staff are being asked to have their say on proposed changes to the NHS Pension Scheme. The government has today launched a public consultation focusing on changes to the scheme which are set to come into force from April 2027.

items.title: Government launches consultation on changes to the NHS Pension Scheme
items.summary: The Government has launched a public consultation seeking views on proposed changes to the NHS Pension Scheme, which are set to come into force from April next year.

items.title: Neighbourhood support teams must be ‘built around nurses’
items.summary: Nursing organisations have stressed that new neighbourhood support teams need to be ‘built around’ district and community nurses who are ‘already doing the work’.

items.title: Call for evidence to determine future of the NHS constitution
items.summary: The Government has launched a public call for evidence to help ‘understand the impact’ of the NHS Constitution for England. This includes asking the public if they support having an NHS constitution at all.

items.title: List-cleansing to have ‘significant’ implications for ARRS budgets, GP leaders warn
items.summary: NHS England’s GP list-cleansing drive will have ‘significant’ implications for additional roles reimbursement scheme (ARRS) budgets, GP leaders and experts have warned.

items.title: ADHD and autism to feature at free Pulse virtual event
items.summary: GPs are invited to a free virtual event next month focussed on ADHD, autism and mental health in primary care.

items.title: NICE approves capsule sponge test for oesophageal cancer in primary care
items.summary: NICE has approved the use of a capsule sponge test to detect oesophageal cancer and Barrett’s oesophagus in primary care and community settings. Two tests – Cytosponge and EndoSign – have been recommended for use on the NHS under new draft guidance.

items.title: QICN award to recognise prescribing students in social care nursing
items.summary: The Queen’s Institute of Community Nursing (QICN) has launched a new academic prize recognising outstanding students undertaking the prescribing programme for adult social care nurses.

items.title: NHS e-learning updated to support people rough sleeping this winter
items.summary: NHS e-learning resources on homelessness have been updated to help GPs and other healthcare staff support people experiencing rough sleeping as part of the Prime Ministers ambition to get people off the streets this winter.

items.title: Resource GPs properly to tackle vaccination decline, House of Lords committee says
items.summary: The Government should review primary care funding for childhood vaccination to tackle declining uptake and address stark inequalities, a report from a House of Lords special inquiry has recommended.

items.title: New ‘neighbourhood support teams’ to keep almost two million out of hospital
items.summary: New neighbourhood support teams aim to keep 1.8 million people out of hospital through ‘dedicated and personalised’ care in the community, the health secretary has announced.

items.title: Patient death raises concerns about community nurses’ access to medical records
items.summary: A coroner has raised concerns about some community nurses’ lack of access to relevant medical records when undertaking invasive procedures following the death of a patient whose catheterisation resulted in haematuria.

items.title: How not to miss: Scabies
items.summary: In the first of a new series looking at conditions that can easily be overlooked or misattributed, GP Dr Keith Hopcroft describes how a case of scabies is initially treated as eczema – and explores some of the other pitfalls that can lead to a delayed diagnosis of this contagious infection Note cases in this series...

items.title: One in three internationally educated nurses ‘never been promoted’ in UK
items.summary: More than a third (34%) of internationally educated nurses and midwives have never been promoted, including one in five (21%) of those with at least 10 years’ experience in the UK, a survey has revealed.

items.title: Redefining obesity would be a weight off my mind
items.summary: Copperfield wonders whether, if changing BMI to waist circumference can make so many people healthier on paper, there are other areas of general practice where a simple change of metric could work wonders Some good news for once. That obesity timebomb they keep talking about may be just a damp squib.

items.title: Improve vaccine access for people with lung conditions, taskforce concludes
items.summary: Too many people with lung conditions are missing out on vital vaccines, according to a taskforce calling for better education and easier access. A survey of more than 2,200 adults with lung conditions commissioned by the Taskforce for Lung Health found many did not see themselves at risk.

items.title: ‘Neighbourhood support teams’ to work with GPs to keep patients out of hospital
items.summary: New ‘neighbourhood support teams’ will work with GPs and provide ‘dedicated and personalised’ care to vulnerable patients to help keep them out of hospital, the health secretary has announced today.

items.title: Practice nurse shortages undermining childhood vaccination efforts, Lords warn
items.summary: A shortage of nurses working in general practice means those among the workforce have less time to speak to parents about childhood vaccinations and is ultimately contributing to falling immunisation rates, a report has warned.

items.title: GMC ‘erroneously’ gave identifiable FtP data to national newspaper
items.summary: The GMC has ‘erroneously’ shared doctors’ personal identifiable data with a national newspaper, including their names and details of allegations against them, the BMA has said.

items.title: Government urged to introduce maximum waiting times for CAMHS by 2028
items.summary: The Government should introduce maximum waiting times from the point of referral for Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) by 2028, a Government review has recommended.

items.title: How this nurse leader is taking primary care beyond the surgery walls
items.summary: We caught up with the Nurse/Nursing Team of the Year shortlist ahead of this year’s General Practice Awards, taking place on 4 December at the Novotel London West in Hammersmith.

items.title: Two funded innovation programmes open to primary care and community nurses
items.summary: The Queen’s Institute of Community Nursing (QICN) has two funded innovation opportunities open to primary care and community nurses wanting to help improve the health and wellbeing of others.

items.title: GPs should not issue long-term fit notes from next year, recommends landmark review
items.summary: GPs should no longer have responsibility for issuing fit notes for long-term sickness absence, according to a major review of youth unemployment in the UK. Alan Milburn’s report, published today, said long-term fit note responsibility should be moved ‘out of general practice’ from 2027.

items.title: Renewed call for long Covid recognition as nurses suffer ‘debilitating effects’ six years on
items.summary: A nursing union has renewed calls for the government to formally recognise long Covid as nurses continue to suffer ‘debilitating effects’ six years after the pandemic began.

items.title: Coroner flags risk of deaths from nurse shortages
items.summary: An inquest into the death of an 83-year-old man whose hip operation was repeatedly cancelled has prompted a coroner to warn that nursing shortages in the NHS could cost more lives.

items.title: GP willingness to use A&G depends on it being ‘timely and clinically useful’
items.summary: The willingness of GPs to use advice and guidance (A&G) depends on whether they receive timely and clinically useful responses, researchers have found.

items.title: Letter calls for patient needs to be prioritised over cost in continence care
items.summary: Continence care must be driven by patient needs and outcomes instead of costs, an open letter signed by the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) and others has urged.

items.title: Up to £6m saved through GP list-cleansing to be returned to ‘most impacted’ practices
items.summary: Government officials have confirmed that up to £6m saved from GP list-cleansing will be returned to ‘practices most impacted’ by the process, the BMA has revealed.

items.title: ‘We can leave the surgery, but can we ever escape our patients?’
items.summary: Dr Burnt Out on the occupational hazard that is being recognised by your patients outside the GP surgery ‘Hello doctor.’ These are two words that you do not necessarily want to hear when you are out and about doing your daily business.

items.title: UK-wide framework to ‘strengthen and celebrate’ nurses’ contribution to public health
items.summary: A new UK-wide framework focused on the contribution of nurses in public health hopes to provide a ‘common language’ to describe, strengthen and celebrate the impact of the profession.

items.title: ‘Now is the time to build on nurses’ public health legacy and leadership’
items.summary: England’s deputy chief public health nurse Professor Jamie Waterall explores how nurses and midwives can build on their public health legacy, using a new UK-wide framework to strengthen leadership, tackle health inequalities and help more people live well for longer.

items.title: HRT prescribing rose 12% last year but inequalities persist
items.summary: Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) prescribing in England has risen by 12%, however the statistic comes amid warnings patients face an ‘unfair postcode lottery’ over access.

items.title: Over 300 reports of ‘unauthorised access’ to medical records made this year
items.summary: The Information Commission’s Office (ICO) is urging NHS England to tackle unauthorised access to patient records, after it revealed it received over 300 reports of ‘unauthorised access’ from health organisations so far this year.

items.title: BMA must support GP practices who want to leave GMS, says NI LMCs
items.summary: LMC representatives at the BMA’s annual NI LMCs conference voted through a motion calling on the BMA to support practices in leaving the GMS contract and ‘implement a plan B’.

items.title: More health and social care workers to be balloted on strike action in Northern Ireland
items.summary: Around 4,000 health and social care workers in Northern Ireland are to be balloted on industrial action amid an ongoing dispute over pay, the union Unite has announced. Unite will ballot its members across 10 employers in Northern Ireland from Monday 23 November until Monday 14 December.

items.title: Only a clear national scope of practice can set safe limits for physician associates, says BMA
items.summary: The BMA has published new ‘red lines’ for physician associates (PAs), which say only a ‘clear’ national scope of practice can set ‘safe limits’ for their work.

items.title: Oral thrush: what nurses need to know
items.summary: Oral thrush is often managed as a minor ailment, but recurrent episodes can signal underlying issues such as medicines-related harm, raised blood sugars or immunosuppression.

items.title: New life-extending anal cancer treatment available on NHS, NICE confirms
items.summary: A life-extending advanced anal cancer treatment has been approved by NICE and is available immediately on the NHS. It is estimated around 250 people in England are set to benefit from the new targeted treatment for anal cancer which has spread and cannot be removed through surgery.

items.title: Moving to new obesity definition could prevent widescale ‘misdiagnosis’
items.summary: Moving to an updated measure of obesity that goes beyond body mass index (BMI) could save the NHS time and money through avoiding misdiagnosis, UK researchers have concluded. Two separate studies have shown poor performance of BMI as an indicator of health across adults in the UK and internationally.

items.title: Nurses urged to ‘think type 1’ this World Diabetes Day
items.summary: To mark World Diabetes Day, Diabetes UK’s Katie Bareford urges nurses and healthcare professionals to ‘think type 1’ and test immediately when children present with any of the 4Ts, as rates of life-threatening diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) at diagnosis reach an eight-year high.

items.title: Nurse struck off after working under influence of alcohol and failing to administer medication
items.summary: A care home nurse who worked while under the influence of alcohol, failed to administer medications and threatened to ‘hunt down and kill’ a colleague is to be struck off. Rupesh Patel was an agency nurse working across three different care homes across Suffolk and Essex at the time of the incidents in 2022 –...

items.title: Care workers set to spend less time travelling between visits under new government plans
items.summary: Care workers are set to spend less time travelling between visits under new government plans to organise social care around local neighbourhoods.

items.title: ‘Being a GP doesn’t prepare you for a terminal diagnosis’
items.summary: Facing a prognosis of less than a year, Dr Grant Ingrams reflects on the realities of terminal cancer and the lessons he hopes fellow GPs will take from his experience 22 October 2025 started like any other Wednesday for me.

items.title: Microsoft outage disrupts patient prescriptions and GP practice systems
items.summary: GP practices have reported a wave of disruption to IT systems, prescriptions and patient referrals amid an ongoing global Microsoft outage.

items.title: Social care to be commissioned around neighbourhoods
items.summary: Social care will be commissioned around local neighbourhoods in parallel to neighbourhood health services, the Government has announced.

items.title: GP antibiotic prescribing drops further but drug resistance still rising
items.summary: GPs have further reduced antibiotic prescribing, but ongoing rising antimicrobial resistance means more work is needed, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has concluded.

items.title: GPs report disruption to IT systems and referrals amid Microsoft outage
items.summary: GP practices across the UK are reporting disruption to IT systems and referrals amid an ongoing global Microsoft outage. Practices have been notifying patients that the outage is causing issues in receiving and replying to emails, as well as delays in receiving and processing hospital correspondence and referrals.

items.title: BMA urges NHS England to ‘immediately’ halt GP practice list cleansing
items.summary: The BMA’s GP committee has called on the Government to ‘immediately’ halt a national patient list-cleansing exercise and to ‘begin urgent discussions’ over the issue.

items.title: General practice staff in Wales trained to use AI tool
items.summary: General practice staff in Wales were among more than 6,000 NHS Wales employees to receive training on using the artificial intelligence (AI) tool Microsoft Copilot in their everyday work.

items.title: Success of new Northern Ireland GP contract depends on investment in nursing, says RCN
items.summary: The success of a new GP contract in Northern Ireland depends on ‘sufficient investment’ in the entire primary care workforce, including nurses, a union has said.

items.title: Data protection regulator receives more than 300 reports of patient record snooping
items.summary: The UK’s data protection regulator has received more than 300 reports of unauthorised access to patient records from health sector organisations so far this year.

items.title: Key questions on lung cancer: recognition and referral
items.summary: In the first of a two-part series, GP cancer lead Dr Esther Appleby and consultant respiratory physician Dr Thomas Simpson answer key questions on recognising and investigating suspected lung cancer in general practice. Complete the full module on Pulse 365 today.

items.title: Overall global sum down by £139m as over one million GP patients removed from lists
items.summary: New NHS England figures showed more than a million patients have now been removed from GP practice lists in England since a nationwide list-cleansing exercise began last October.

items.title: A clear message on vaping: holding two truths at once
items.summary: While new evidence strengthens the case for nicotine vapes as an effective smoking cessation aid, a major review highlights the risks for children and young people. In this clinical feature, Darush Attar-Zadeh and Nazir Hussain stress that for nurses the task is to communicate both messages clearly at the same time.

items.title: GPs keen to add data to Palantir platform, company suggested to health minister
items.summary: US tech company Palantir contacted a health minister about the benefits of adding GP patient data to its national health data tool, documents have revealed.

items.title: Defect notice for blood pressure medication with strength typo
items.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has issued a defect notice for a blood pressure medication which states the incorrect dose on its packaging.

items.title: Mildly low platelets: what should GPs do next?
items.summary: Clinical conundrum: In the next in our series, consultant haematologist Dr Priya Sriskandarajah advises on how to manage a female patient presenting with mildly low platelets on repeat testing who feels well but reports easy bruising A 38-year-old female is called in to discuss repeat blood tests.

items.title: UKHSA concerned over ‘low uptake’ of pharmacy MenB jab offer
items.summary: Less than one in three eligible 18- and 19-year-olds have had a first dose of the free MenB vaccine which is currently being offered in pharmacies. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said this meant more than 580,000 students in this age group had not yet come forward. The government agency said it was concerned...

items.title: Minister assures NHS workforce plan will address need for more community nurses
items.summary: The highly anticipated NHS workforce plan will set out plans for boosting the community nursing workforce, a minister has assured. It comes as several concerns have been raised around a sharp decline in nurses working across the community – including a 49% reduction in district nurses between 2009 and June 2026.

items.title: Easier access to primary care is putting ‘extreme demand’ on waiting list, NHSE says
items.summary: Easier access to primary care is leading to extreme demand for services, NHS England has said. It comes as figures show a record number of patients have been referred to the waiting list for elective care.

items.title: Last chance to register for free Pulse virtual event with sessions on COPD and diabetes
items.summary: GPs have less than a week to register for a free two-day virtual event in November which will feature a talk from NHS England’s national clinical director for prescribing.

items.title: Upcoming Nursing in Practice virtual event to focus on diabetes and respiratory
items.summary: Nurses working in primary care and community settings are being invited to attend a free virtual event focused on diabetes and respiratory conditions next month. Nursing in Practice Virtual: Diabetes and Respiratory takes place on Thursday 3 December.

items.title: Stopping GLP-1s associated with increased risk of heart attack and stroke, study finds
items.summary: Stopping GLP-1 treatment is associated with a substantially increased risk of heart attack, stroke or death, a new study has found.

items.title: Room tidying, list cleansing, dirty tricks
items.summary: Copperfield on how NHS England’s latest attempts to squeeze general practice won’t result in less work for GPs First NHSE came for our patients. Now they’re coming for our waiting rooms. Next it’ll be our lunch money. To explain.

items.title: Drug-facilitated sexual assault: preparing nurses to spot the signs
items.summary: Victims of organised drug-facilitated sexual assault often have no idea what has happened, so it can fall to nurses and other healthcare professionals to notice the signs and ask the right questions – but are they ready?

items.title: Rate of babies born with congenital anomalies in Wales falls
items.summary: The rate of babies born with congenital anomalies in Wales has steadily fallen over recent years, a new report has revealed.

items.title: NHS Property Services installs sensors in 150 GP practices to ‘identify unused space’
items.summary: Exclusive NHS Property Services has installed ‘utilisation sensors’ in around 150 GP practices across England to track how much clinical space is being used, Pulse has learnt.

items.title: BMA pauses consultant strikes as it enters formal negotiations with Government
items.summary: Hospital consultant strikes planned for later this month have been paused, as the BMA and the Government agreed to enter formal negotiations over pay and working conditions.

items.title: RCGP questions NHS England’s claim that GP consultation rooms are underused
items.summary: The RCGP has disputed a claim that GP consultation rooms are underused, arguing that any estimate around practice premises needs to ‘reflect how general practice actually operates’.

items.title: How this nursing associate is breaking down barriers to care for vulnerable patients
items.summary: We caught up with the Nurse/Nursing Team of the Year shortlist ahead of this year’s General Practice Awards, taking place on 4 December at the Novotel London West in Hammersmith.

items.title: Nurse shortages and lack of workforce planning threaten social care reform
items.summary: A growing shortage of registered nurses in social care is creating challenges for specialist providers, while the absence of a long-term workforce plan risks exacerbating pressures in the sector, a report published by the Casey Commission has warned.

items.title: ‘Going into private general practice saved me from leaving medicine altogether’
items.summary: After suffering burnout from eight years as a GP partner in the NHS, Dr Oliver Denton’s move into private practice helped him find his way back to what he loved about the job in the first place From day one as a GP trainee in Gloucestershire my goal was to become a partner.

items.title: Cold-health alert issued for North West and West Midlands regions
items.summary: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued its first cold-health alert of the 2026/27 winter season – warning that low temperatures can result in increased use of health care services.

items.title: ‘Enhanced’ Band 7 health visitor role created after long-running strike action
items.summary: A ‘new and distinct’ Band 7 specialist health visitor role has been created in Wales following nine months of industrial action.

items.title: iHV issues training guide for perinatal and infant mental health
items.summary: A new brochure to provide nurses, health visitors and other practitioners with specialist training information on perinatal and infant mental health has been launched by the Institute of Health Visiting (iHV).

items.title: Civil servant convicted of fraud for holding multiple full-time Government and NHS jobs
items.summary: A former civil servant has been convicted of fraud for obtaining and holding multiple full-time Government jobs at the same time, including at the Department of Health and Social Care and at one NHS trust.

items.title: Long Covid linked to 14% higher risk of developing high blood pressure
items.summary: People diagnosed with long Covid had a 14% higher risk of developing high blood pressure than those without the condition, a new study involving more than 1.2 million adults has found.

items.title: A&G and referrals to remain ‘separate options’ within single point of access, GPs told
items.summary: GP practices in one area have been told they will be able to continue sending advice and guidance (A&G) requests and referrals as separate options via ‘multiple’ single points of access within each trust, covering individual specialties and subspecialties.

items.title: BMA accepts Northern Ireland GP contract offer putting an end to collective action
items.summary: The BMA in Northern Ireland has reached a deal with the Government for the 2026/27 GP contract, including an additional £20m in each of the next two years to support neighbourhood health reforms and ‘improve access’.

items.title: Care home nurses vaccinating residents to help ‘take burden off’ GP practices
items.summary: Care home nurses in Lancashire and South Cumbria are administering vaccinations directly to residents and staff under a new innovative programme.

items.title: One in three people put off GP appointments due to work pressures, Healthwatch finds
items.summary: More than one in three workers in England delayed or avoided going to a GP appointment in the last year because of work commitment or difficulty getting time off, a new survey has found. The research commissioned by Healthwatch England also found that the figure rose to 50% among employees on zero-hours contracts.

items.title: Success of winter plan will ‘rely on whole general practice workforce’
items.summary: Government funding to boost winter capacity in primary care services will only deliver success if practice nurses are placed at the “heart of planning and decision-making”, a union has warned.

items.title: NHSE chair suggests GP practices turn waiting areas into consulting rooms
items.summary: The NHS England chair has suggested GP practices could turn waiting areas into consultation rooms, amid an ongoing review into how the GP estate is used.

items.title: ‘I’m warning my patients about the single patient record – are you?’
items.summary: Dr Paul O’Reilly makes a case against the proposed single patient record, warning that GPs may no longer be able to protect their patients by losing the data controller role As they perceive it, the greatest threat to the liberty of my patients is the efficiency of what they typically experience as a malign…

items.title: Interview: NMC entering ‘new era’ as Paul Rees vows to ‘turn regulator around once and for all’
items.summary: In an exclusive interview with Nursing in Practice, Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) chief executive and registrar Paul Rees reflects on the challenges and changes seen at the regulator over the last year – from the increased registration fee, to lessons learnt from the Letby case, record fitness to practise…

items.title: Patients urged to get vaccinated as data shows flu activity is ‘increasing’
items.summary: Patients eligible for the flu vaccination are being urged by Public Health Wales to get vaccinated as soon as possible following evidence that the flu is circulating.

items.title: Nurse-led clinics could benefit from £40m reallocated funding for GP practices
items.summary: The government has announced that £40m of general practice funding will be reallocated to help provide ‘additional care’ for patients considered most at risk of becoming seriously unwell this winter.

items.title: Money saved through GP list-cleansing drive to fund £40m winter programme
items.summary: A programme for practices to identify and provide additional care to frail patients will be funded via money saved through NHS England’s GP list cleansing drive.

items.title: Practice nurses urged to champion veteran health scheme
items.summary: In the lead up to Remembrance Day, practice nurses are being encouraged to champion a health scheme to provide the best possible care and treatment for Armed Forces veterans.

items.title: Unions and MPs warn that GP nurses will be ‘left behind’ on pay
items.summary: Calls by some ministers and unions to ringfence GP nursing salaries have gone unanswered by the government and NHS England despite their recommendation to boost pay for GPs and doctors.
